author: ValWood
body:
S. pombe cannot utilise mannitol or sorbitol and is therefore unlikely to reduce them

author: ValWood
body: I have forgotten how to tag Rhea, there is no label

author: ValWood
body:
This follows from the natural history. Honeybee honey is a primary habitat for S. pombe, and this has negligible mannitol. Sorbose appears to generally not be naturally produced. In fact, all of the annotations to both terms appear to derive from a single paper
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P87219/entry

author: Antonialock
body:
These entries are annotated to the funfam and have EXP annotation to GO:0050085 | mannitol 2-dehydrogenase (NADP+) activity: P0C0Y5 P87219 Q8NK50 Q6CEE9 P0C0Y4

I see you added a NOT to this process for pombe. I'm pretty sure accounting for NOTs will be implemented. I will double check

As for the rhea etc uniprot annotation - I fixed the pombe annotation back in October, I'm pretty sure it will be in our next release.

author: Antonialock
body: I found an example of a different function for proteins in this funfam group. Candida parapsilosis has 3 proteins that are carbonyl reductases https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2011/ob/c0ob00938e I can annotate these and the annotation should move up to oxidoreductase....

author: Antonialock
body: We have talked about "black listing" entries with NOT GO annotation. In any case I curated 4 carbonyl reductases that have this signature so I presume the rule will be augmented. Iw ill close this since I think I have fixed it but I am keeping tabs on what issues to check back on once we have gone through an update.
